text:
morgan: Heads-up — spotted a weird eviction pattern on Qwen-MQA runs with longcontexts (>32k). Memory climbs steadily then drops like a sneeze, repeatable when rope_scale changes from 1.0 -> 0.5. Logs attached below. :thinking:

anita: ugh, sneeze pattern? can you paste the alloc traces? sounds like fragmentation + batch alignment. :eyes:

morgan: here are the minimal traces from the failing run (trimmed):

```
[2026-02-23T15:02:34Z] kv_alloc slab=3 size=65536 seq=0x1a2b3c id=slot42
[2026-02-23T15:02:34Z] kv_map put slot=42 page=2304 rope_scale=1.0
[2026-02-23T15:07:12Z] kv_evict victim=2304 reason=compact_reclaim
[2026-02-23T15:07:13Z] kv_alloc slab=3 size=65536 seq=0x1a2b3d id=slot43
[2026-02-23T15:07:13Z] kv_map put slot=43 page=2304 rope_scale=0.5
[2026-02-23T15:11:00Z] kv_evict victim=2304 reason=forced_evict
```

morgan: notice same page gets reused but different rope_scale, eviction spikes align with batch flushes.

devon: can you repro with a deterministic workload? maybe batching heuristic + kernel switch triggers different per-token growth.

morgan: yes repro script attached — sequence of 40k tokens, interspersed short replies to force KV churn. I reduced concurrency to 1 to avoid noise.

kai: did you check kernel selection logs? if we swap to the optimized matmul kernel, KV footprint can change due to transitional buffers.

morgan: good call. here's the kernel telemetry around the sneeze times:

```
[telemetry] seq=... kernel=matmul_opt_v2 -> matmul_generic at 15:07:12 (fallback)
[telemetry] batch_size=1 -> 8 at 15:07:12
[telemetry] kv_cache_pages=72 -> 86 at 15:07:12
```

anita: so two correlated things: kernel fallback + batching jump. batching heuristics may be bumping batch_size when latency SLOs are loose, which increases intermediate activation sizes and forces eviction.

devon: also Qwen's MQA has denser KV mapping per head group, rope scaling changes the key distribution across pages. mixing rope_scale variants in same page may increase fragmentation.

morgan: I ran a profiling flamegraph — peak memory frames attached. The hot path is kv_map::insert -> kernel_dispatch_wrapper -> batch_pack

perf-bot: perf alert: mem_growth delta +18% over baseline for run 1768003456. Suggestion: try pinning rope_scale or isolating MQA groups per slab.

kai: proposal: conservative change set to try: 
- force consistent rope_scale per slab (prevent mixed variants in same slab)
- tighten batching heuristic: cap batch growth if page_reuse_ratio < 0.7
- skip matmul_opt_v2 fallback under small-batch transient spikes (investigate root cause)

anita: that sounds reasonable. quick experiment: morgan, can you run two variants: (A) rope_scale pinned per-worker, (B) batching cap disabled but kernel pinned to generic. Need run ids and flamegraphs.

morgan: starting runs now. runA ts=1768003567 pinned-rope, runB ts=1768003723 kernel-generic. will post results in ~10m. :wave:

devon: if runA stabilizes, we should add a heuristic in allocator to avoid mixing pages with incompatible rope_scale metadata. maybe encode rope_scale in page header and skip reuse if mismatch. low-risk check.

morgan: runA done. summary: memory growth flattened, no sneeze events in 3 repeats. runA last mem +2% vs baseline. flamegraph shows reduced kv_map churn.

morgan: runB (kernel-generic) also reduced evictions but latency increased ~12ms p50. tradeoff noted.

kai: good. next steps:
- patch allocator: page header rope_scale tag + reuse check (devon)
- adjust batching heuristic to consider page_reuse_ratio (anita)
- monitor for regressions on Llama / Mistral (morgan)

anita: will prototype batching cap today. devon can you own allocator tag change?

devon: yes I will open a small PR and include a stress test that mixes rope_scale values to ensure no regressions. will include micro-benchmark showing allocation churn reduction.

perf-bot: note added to ticket INF-8721 linking traces and flamegraphs.

morgan: thanks all — huge reduction in noise. leaving here for now, will follow up with PR links. :thumbsup:
